sources.entry: JET Pilot - Open-source Kubernetes desktop client for working across clusters, namespaces and cloud accounts, with multi-cluster views, a resource graph, structured logs and a built-in kubectl terminal.

summary.one_liner: JET Pilot is a free, MIT-licensed open-source Kubernetes desktop IDE built with Rust and Tauri, combining keyboard-first navigation with a polished mouse-friendly UI.
summary.what_it_does: JET Pilot is a desktop client for managing Kubernetes clusters across multiple kubeconfig files, contexts and namespaces, aggregating resources into tables with Context and Namespace columns. It provides a clusters hub that lists clusters from kubeconfigs and cloud accounts, with support for connecting AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and several other providers. It includes a resource graph, a structured log viewer that parses JSON log lines, a full YAML editor for objects, and a built-in local terminal with kubectl preconfigured for the current context. It also offers GitOps views for Flux and Argo CD, Helm release management, access review (RBAC) queries, and usage charts from Prometheus or metrics-server. The README says it uses existing kubeconfig files and kubectl and has no account or telemetry.
use_cases: manage multiple Kubernetes clusters from one app
view logs across all pods of a workload
inspect how Services, Deployments and Pods relate
edit Kubernetes YAML manifests with apply shortcuts
review who can do what in RBAC
monitor Flux or Argo CD GitOps applications
install and upgrade Helm charts with a diff
notable: Keyboard-first command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) with fuzzy search for switching contexts and namespaces
Built-in terminal with kubectl preconfigured without modifying the user's own kubeconfig
Production guardrails: protected clusters require typing the cluster name before destructive actions; read-only clusters block changes
Structured log viewer that parses JSON log fields and supports facet filtering
Supports custom themes from VS Code, Sublime Text and TextMate
caveats: macOS build is not notarized by Apple, so the quarantine flag must be removed manually when installing the .dmg (Homebrew tap handles this)
Windows installer is not code-signed and may trigger SmartScreen warnings
JET Pilot is no longer in Homebrew's main cask repository and must be installed from its own tap
